correctness.rationale: A fixed point has constant barycentric coordinates on each occupied vertex orbit, so it is parametrized by the complex of unions of compatible orbits, via the orbit barycenters. Arrow reversal has no compatible orbit. For geometric reflection the center is forbidden (opposing arrows on one edge, or incompatible opposite signs on adjacent edges); for sign-preserving reflection it is retained. Away from the center, compatibility is precisely the adjacency rule on the left half. This gives the two PL identifications, including the empty R-fixed space when n=2. The two endpoint-arrow stars are cones whose intersection is the (n−2)-edge complex; the two-point and two-component bases give the sphere recurrence. An invariant face on k vertices in h orbits contributes (−1)^(k−1)(−1)^(k−h)=(−1)^(h−1) to the augmented trace, including the empty face. Taking reduced Euler characteristics of the folded complexes gives the claimed integral signs. Rational orbit chains after subdivision are coinvariants, exact by averaging, and both signs are trivial exactly when m is divisible by four. The frozen finite checker and output were inspected, not executed; the proof does not rely on those finite outcomes.
